title: Taq Kasra (Taq-i Kisra), Ctesiphon
summary: The great vaulted hall (ayvan) of Taq Kasra at Ctesiphon, on the Tigris, is the surviving part of a Sasanian palace. Its date is disputed between the reign of Shapur I and the 6th century CE. Floods in 1888 destroyed a third of the standing ruin; Iraq restored it in the 1970s.

uncertainty.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica reports a tradition giving Shapur I (r. 241-72) and a stylistic case for the 6th century (Khosrow I); Amusing Planet says late 6th century. So the start lies between 241 and 600. End is the present: the ruin still stands.

phases.description: Built between the reign of Shapur I (r. 241-72) and the 6th century CE; the date is disputed (Encyclopaedia Iranica).
The pages opened give no dated changes between building and 1888; Amusing Planet says floods later destroyed the rest of Ctesiphon.
Floods of 1888 destroyed one third of the standing ruin (Encyclopaedia Iranica).
Iraq completed restoration of the south wing in 1972; reconstruction of the collapsed north wing began in 1975.

reviewer_note: Shape block (facade with arched iwan). Iranica gives the facade 35 m high and the iwan 25.5 m wide; Amusing Planet gives a 37 m high, 26 m wide arch. These differ (they may measure different points) and I used Iranica first. Date is contested (Shapur I vs 6th century), so the 241-600 construction span is wide. The 600-1888 intact phase is a bridge; the Iranica article is dated 2017 and does not say who restored what after 1975. Pin is an OSM node for the iwan.
